- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is flat or slightly rising, model tends to underpredict — adjust upward by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and forecast is rising, model often overestimates — cap upward slope at 1–2% per day or reduce by 3–5% if sentiment persists.
- After sharp spikes in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model frequently overshoots — apply “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending, model often fails to mean-revert — force a slight downward correction if price deviates >2% from 14-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price when sentiment is positive — add 3–7% bias correction if sentiment > 0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative after a positive streak, model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 1–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes or reverses.
